The Healing of the Man Born Blind

Icons

Scriptural scenes

The Healing of the Man Born Blind

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

John 9:1–7

John 9:35–38

King James Version · Scripture previews

The Healing of the Man Born Blind depicts the encounter narrated in John 9. The OCA reads the miracle in relation to Christ’s creative work and the movement from physical sight toward recognition of Him.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6

What is depicted

The pictured Healing of the Man Born Blind is a historical work by Emmanuel Tzanes dated 1686. Christ approaches the blind man among witnesses, with the narrative setting extended behind them. The attribution and date come from the artwork’s exact catalogue record.

[2] Exact artwork file: Description, Creator, Date, Credit and licence fields; complete downloaded image visually compared

History and tradition

The OCA emphasizes Christ’s answer that the man’s blindness is not explained by assigning a personal sin to him or his parents. It connects the making of clay with the creation of humanity from earth. That typological explanation is attributed to the published church account, while the Gospel passage itself remains separate.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 3, 4, 5, 6

Published explanation

And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth.

And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?

Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.

I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.

As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.

When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,

And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.

[3] John 9:1–7
